text.tspan: Since there are 9 observations, which is odd, the median is the 5
The range is the difference between the highest score and the lowest score, so
There are 9 scores, so the median is the 5
So far, the descriptive statistics we have found would describe the two groups as identical. They
have the same mean, same median, and same range. But are the data spread out the same? See
The two groups appear very different in how they are dispersed. Group #1 appears to be very
spread out, with all data far from the mean = 5. But the data in Group #2 appears mostly clustered
around the mean = 5, except for the smallest and largest values. Overall, Group #1 is widely
dispersed, while Group #2 is closely grouped. The statistics for mean, median, and range do not
reflect the difference in the dispersion patterns, and thus do not describe the data well enough.
Range is not sufficient to describe the variation because it considers only the highest and lowest
values. We need a statistic that measures the
distance from the mean, considering all the
data values, not just the highest and lowest.
